questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the final opportunity to review the date, time, and meeting settings before the event is officially created.
questions.check: What title, date, time, guests and video link does the event show before Save?
questions.say_example: Saving it. <Private class with Sarah>, <Thursday 3 to 4>, Meet link attached, guest <Sarah>. Nothing goes out until the send prompt.

questions.question: Do you want to throw away the unsaved meeting?
questions.why: The screen shows a confirmation dialog asking to discard unsaved changes, which determines whether the current meeting setup is permanently deleted.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to decide whether to abandon the incomplete meeting invitation or return to finish scheduling it.
questions.check: Does the page show a dialog asking to discard unsaved changes?
questions.say_example: A box asked whether to throw away the meeting I was setting up. I kept it.

questions.question: Do you want to save the meeting without any guests?
questions.why: The prompt warns that saving without invitees means participants will not be able to see the group chat before and after the meeting.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide whether to add invitees immediately to ensure they have full access to the meeting's chat history.
questions.check: Does the prompt warn about saving without invitees?
questions.say_example: Saved without guests, as you named none. You'll share the link yourself.

questions.question: Is the Google Meet link actually on the saved calendar event?
questions.why: Checking the event details pop-up for the 'Join with Google Meet' button and link confirms that the meeting was properly generated for your invitees.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the reassurance of personally verifying that the correct video call link is attached to your specific calendar invitation.
questions.check: Does the saved event show a 'Join with Google Meet' button or a meeting link?
questions.say_example: The saved event has no video link. Guests would get a calendar entry with nowhere to click. Adding one now.

questions.question: Does the meeting link in the event details match the one you originally generated?
questions.why: The meeting link shown for the birthday call at 08:00 is completely different from the link generated during the event creation at 11:05.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the guarantee that they and their invitees will actually end up in the same virtual meeting room.
questions.check: Does the link or meeting ID on the saved event match the one shown when it was created?
questions.say_example: The link on the saved event isn't the one I made a minute ago. I'll use the saved one, since that's what the guests got.

questions.question: Do you want to check the meeting ID and passcode before starting?
questions.why: Tapping the scheduled meeting reveals its specific details, including the meeting ID and passcode, which might be needed for verification or sharing.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to verify the exact meeting credentials or retrieve the passcode before launching the call.
questions.check: Does the meeting detail page show the meeting ID and passcode?
questions.say_example: Noted meeting ID <123 456 789> and passcode <abc123>.

children.label: Invite the participants
children.note: the invite is almost never sent inside the product. 4.1 or 4.2 on nearly every host - before the meeting from the saved details, or inside it from the Add others dialog or the Invite button. 4.3 on the two that edit what they copied. then 4.4 or 4.5 outside the product, where the corpus shows it at all. 4.6 from inside the meeting on Meet and Zoom. 4.7 on the Calendar and Teams routes, where the product sends. 4.8 on 6Yc8 and the .ics offers. 4.9 wherever a dial-in block is on screen. 4.10 on the two that switch to the recipient's inbox.

questions.question: How do you want to invite participants to the meeting?
questions.why: The dialog provides options to either copy the joining link to share manually or send an automated email invitation directly to specific contacts.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose control over the communication channel used to invite guests, as the agent might send an automated email instead of letting you share the link via your preferred messaging app.
questions.check: Which invite options does the dialog show, and did a 'Link copied' message appear after the copy?
questions.say_example: Copied the link to share. Nobody has been emailed.

questions.question: Do you need the meeting passcode written down for your guests?
questions.why: The invite dialog displays a meeting password, which you must share with participants so they can securely access the call.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally verify the meeting's security settings and note the exact password your guests will need to join.
questions.check: Does the invitation show a meeting password or passcode?
questions.say_example: Noted the passcode from the invitation. Guests need it.

questions.question: Are the meeting details in the invitation correct before you copy it?
questions.why: Checking the topic, time, and access details ensures you are sharing the correct meeting information with your invitees.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to verify the meeting topic and schedule before the invitation is shared.
questions.check: Do the topic, date and time in the invitation text match the meeting that was scheduled?
questions.say_example: The invitation says <Wednesday 2pm>. You scheduled <Thursday 3pm>. I won't send it. Opening the right meeting.

questions.question: Which parts of the invitation should you copy for guests?
questions.why: The modal displays a long block of text, so selecting only the essential link, ID, and password prevents overwhelming your guests with unnecessary dial-in numbers.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to curate the invitation text to ensure it only includes the most relevant joining details for your specific guests.
questions.check: Does the invitation text include a link, a meeting ID, a passcode, and dial-in numbers?
questions.say_example: Trimmed the invite to the link, ID and passcode. Left out the dial-in numbers.

questions.question: Does the email draft have the link, meeting ID and passcode in it?
questions.why: The screen shows a Gmail compose window where you must choose how to paste the clipboard contents to share the meeting link with your invitees.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the chance to manually place and review the pasted meeting details within your custom message.
questions.check: Does the email body show the meeting link, the meeting ID and the passcode?
questions.say_example: The email has the link but no passcode. Guests couldn't get in without it. Adding it.

questions.question: Is the invitation email addressed and worded right before it goes out?
questions.why: The screen shows a new email draft with the pasted Zoom invitation, requiring a decision on the recipient address and subject line to successfully deliver the meeting details.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means the agent chooses the communication channel and recipient addresses, potentially sending the invitation to the wrong person or using an inappropriate method.
questions.check: What recipients, subject and body does the message show before send?
questions.say_example: Ready to send the invitation to <sarah@mail.com>. Subject <Private class Thursday>. Link and passcode inside. Say send.

questions.question: Are you ready to send the meeting link to the contact?
questions.why: The WhatsApp input field contains the pasted Messenger room link, meaning the next step is to send the invitation.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to verify the recipient or add a personal greeting to the invitation.
questions.check: Does the chat box show the meeting link, and which contact's chat is open?
questions.say_example: The link is typed into your chat with <Priya>. Say send, and it goes.

questions.question: Is anyone you want to invite blocked by the meeting's organization-only rule?
questions.why: The dialog displays the meeting link alongside a specific domain restriction, requiring you to decide if your intended guests meet the access criteria.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to evaluate whether the specific domain restriction on this meeting aligns with the people you actually need to invite.
questions.check: Does the 'Add people' dialog show a restriction, such as only people in a named domain can join?
questions.say_example: This meeting only lets in <acme.com> accounts. <Tom's> address is <gmail>, so he couldn't get in.

questions.question: Do you want to send invitation emails to the Google Calendar guests?
questions.why: The screen displays a prompt asking whether to send invitation emails to the added guests, offering options to send, not send, or dismiss.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses control over whether their guests receive an immediate email notification about the newly scheduled meeting.
questions.check: Does the page show a prompt asking whether to send invitation emails, and which guests are listed?
questions.say_example: The calendar wants to email the invite to <Sarah> and <Tom>. Say send, or say don't send and I'll save it quietly.

questions.question: Is the outside email address spelled exactly right before the invite goes out?
questions.why: The system initially shows 'No results found' while typing, requiring you to enter the full email address to trigger the specific 'Invite' dropdown option.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to verify the exact spelling of the external email address before the invitation is sent.
questions.check: Does the typed address match the one the person gave, letter for letter, and does the page show 'No results found'?
questions.say_example: I typed <sarah@gmial.com>. You gave <sarah@gmail.com>. Fixing it before the invite goes out.

questions.question: Which calendar service do you want to add this meeting to?
questions.why: The meeting details page offers options to add the event to Google, Outlook, or Yahoo calendars, which determines where your schedule and join link are saved.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Letting an agent choose the calendar service could result in the event being saved to an account you do not actively monitor.
questions.check: Which calendar options does the page list?
questions.say_example: Added it to your <Google> calendar, the one you use.

questions.question: Do you want to give the meeting app the account access it's asking for?
questions.why: The screen asks you to select an account and warns that you may be sharing sensitive information by granting Zoom access to your Google Account.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose control over which personal account is linked to the application and the opportunity to review or deny the requested data permissions.
questions.check: Does the page ask to choose an account and grant the meeting app access, and what access does it list?
questions.say_example: Zoom wants access to your Google account, <you@gmail.com>. It lists <calendar and contacts>. Say allow, or say skip and I'll copy the link into your calendar by hand.

children.label: Enter the meeting
children.note: guests run 5.1 to 5.7 - 5.1 always, 5.2 once, then one of 5.3 to 5.5, with 5.6 when the link did not carry the ID (6fIY) and 5.7 when there is no account (3Bje, 8bF-, QOUw). hosts of a scheduled meeting run 5.9; instant hosts arrive from 2. 5.8 on Zoom and Teams and Messenger - never on Meet. then 5.10 on every keeper that reaches the pre-join screen, then 5.11. 5.12 is where three guest joins end. 5.13 on the keepers that check what they are in - and in 8bF- guests cannot see the title before admission.

questions.question: Do the sender and the link in this email look like the meeting you expect?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to visually verify the meeting's sender and URL details before launching the video call.
questions.check: Who is the email from, what domain does the join link point to, and does the mail app flag the sender as unknown?

questions.question: Which of the two time zones in this invitation is the real meeting time?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to clarify the actual meeting time before sending out an incorrectly scheduled invite.

questions.question: How do you want to join from this invitation, the button, the link, or the code?
questions.why: The email displays both a direct URL and a meeting ID with a passcode, offering different ways to access the call.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the choice of whether to join instantly via the provided link or manually through the app using the meeting credentials.
questions.check: Does the email show a join button, a link, and a meeting ID with a passcode?
questions.say_example: Opened the join link from the email.

questions.question: Do you want to reply yes to this invitation?
questions.why: The screen displays an email invitation for a 'Top secret meeting' from Kevin Stratvert, requiring you to verify the event details and confirm your attendance.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means an agent might accept an incorrect or unwanted meeting invitation without understanding your actual schedule and priorities.
questions.check: Does the invitation show Yes, No and Maybe buttons, and which is selected?
questions.say_example: Left the RSVP unanswered. You didn't ask me to.

questions.question: Which scheduled meeting on your calendar do you want to join?
questions.why: The calendar displays multiple upcoming events like the 'Weekly check-in meeting' and 'Sales Team Meeting', so the exact meeting to attend must be identified.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide which specific meeting from your schedule to join at this moment.
questions.check: Which events does the calendar show around the requested time, with titles and times?
questions.say_example: Two meetings near now. <Weekly check-in> at <2>, <Sales team> at <2:30>. Which one?

questions.question: Do the time and organizer on this calendar event match the meeting you meant to join?
questions.why: The calendar event for the 'Demo Class' provides a specific 'Join with Google Meet' button to access the correct video call.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the chance to verify the meeting details, like the time and organizer, before launching the call.
questions.check: What title, time and organizer does the opened event or meeting card show, and do they match the meeting the person named?
questions.say_example: The event I opened is <Demo class> from <Ms Lee> at <2:45>. You said the <3 o'clock with Dr Park>. Wrong one. Looking again.

questions.question: Do you want to join the Teams meeting from this email invitation?
questions.why: The email reading pane displays a 'Join' button for the weekly check-in Teams meeting, which is the direct path to entering the call.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to review the meeting's schedule and sender details before clicking the join link.
questions.check: Does the email show a Join button for the meeting?
questions.say_example: Pressed join in the email. It opened the pre-join screen.

questions.question: Is the link in the browser exactly the one from the invitation?
questions.why: Pasting the URL directly into the browser's address bar is the most direct way to initiate the meeting platform's join flow.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to verify the exact meeting URL and choose which specific browser profile handles the link.
questions.check: Does the address bar show the same link as the invitation, or a shortened or different address?
questions.say_example: The page I landed on isn't the address in the invite. It went through <bit.ly>. Going back and opening the original.

questions.question: There are two meeting links on the page. Which one is the right one?
questions.why: The screen displays a Meet link in the class header banner as well as one in a specific post, presenting two different ways to access the meeting.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to choose whether to join via the persistent class header link or the specific context of the instructor's post.
questions.check: Does the page show more than one meeting link, and are they different?
questions.say_example: This page has two meeting links. The banner one and the post one differ. Using the one in <today's post>. Say banner if that's wrong.

questions.question: Does the page say the meeting link is invalid, expired, or cancelled?
questions.why: If the meeting was cancelled or the link is old, the platform will display an error instead of the pre-join screen, meaning you cannot proceed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent might repeatedly try to join a non-existent meeting instead of notifying you to ask the organizer for a new link.
questions.check: Does the page say the meeting link is invalid, expired, ended, or cancelled?
questions.say_example: The page says this meeting <has ended>. The link won't get you in. Ask <the organizer> for a new one.

questions.question: Does the code typed into the join field match the one in the invitation exactly?
questions.why: The Google Meet homepage provides a specific text field to paste the code from your email, noting that dashes are optional.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the chance to verify the exact meeting code being used to access the call.
questions.check: Does the code in the join field match the meeting ID in the invitation, rather than the passcode or a dial-in number?

questions.question: What meeting ID should I enter?
questions.why: The 'Join' button remains disabled until you input the specific identifier for the meeting you want to attend.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to securely retrieve the correct meeting credentials from your private calendar or email.

questions.question: What passcode do you need to enter to join the meeting?
questions.why: The screen prompts for a meeting passcode, which must be retrieved from the invitation email to successfully join the call.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the security of keeping their meeting access credentials and personal email inbox private.
questions.check: Does the page ask for a passcode, and does the invitation show one?
questions.say_example: Entered the passcode from the invite.

questions.question: Is a whole web address sitting in the meeting code box instead of just the code?
questions.why: If you paste an entire web address into a field that only expects a specific meeting code, the platform may silently reject it or leave the join button disabled until you manually delete the excess text.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to recognize why the system is blocking their join attempt and to manually edit the pasted text down to just the valid code.
questions.check: Does the code field contain 'http' or a full address, and is the Join button disabled?
questions.say_example: The whole link got pasted into the code box, and join stayed grey. Trimming it to just the code.

questions.question: Does the display-name field show your name, not a leftover from someone else?
questions.why: The pre-join screen requires a display name to identify you to others before you can click to enter the meeting.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to choose how your name appears to other attendees and to verify your own readiness before entering the waiting room.
questions.check: What does the name field on the pre-join screen show?
questions.say_example: The name box was filled in as <Charlies Lessons>. That's what everyone would see. Changing it to <your name>.

questions.question: Do you want the browser to remember your display name for future Zoom meetings?
questions.why: The name entry dialog includes a 'Remember my name for future meetings' checkbox, which saves your entered name locally so you don't have to type it again next time.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to decide whether their display name is stored in the browser's local data, which they might want to avoid on a shared computer.
questions.check: Is the 'Remember my name' box checked?
questions.say_example: Left the remember-my-name box unticked.

questions.question: Should the browser open the Teams desktop app?
questions.why: The browser prompt asks for permission to open the meeting in the Teams application, which determines whether the call takes place in the dedicated app or the web browser.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to choose between using the installed desktop application or continuing the meeting directly within the web browser.
questions.check: Does the page show a prompt to open the meeting in the desktop app, with a continue-in-browser option?
questions.say_example: The site tried to open the <Teams> app. I stayed in the browser, where I can still see the call for you. Say app if you'd rather.

questions.question: Should you download the desktop app or continue in the browser?
questions.why: The screen presents options to download the Teams app, open an existing app, or continue in the browser, which dictates whether new software must be installed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to choose whether to install a dedicated application on their device or proceed with the zero-installation browser route.
questions.check: Does the page offer 'Continue on this browser' alongside the app download?
questions.say_example: Continued in the browser. Nothing was downloaded.

questions.question: Do you want to start the meeting from the card on the home screen?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the contextual awareness of seeing their daily schedule and upcoming meetings laid out on the homepage before joining.
questions.check: Does the home screen show the scheduled meeting with a Join or Start button?

questions.check: Is the 'Always show video preview' box checked?

questions.question: How much noise suppression do you want on your mic?

questions.check: What does the microphone dropdown show, and does the page say 'No microphone found' or that the microphone is muted by the system?

questions.check: Which audio options does the dialog show, and which is selected?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the ability to decide whether to participate in the external whiteboard activity or remain solely in the main meeting interface.
questions.check: Does the page show an invitation from another participant to open a whiteboard in a new tab?
questions.say_example: <Charlie> invited everyone to a Miro board in a new tab. I'm staying in the call. Say open it if you want it.

children.label: Record the meeting
children.note: 8.3.1 first - and what it finds decides the rest: local or cloud on Zoom, an admin gate on G Suite, nothing on free Meet. 8.3.2 only in 0Qvm, outside the product. then 8.3.3, and 8.3.4 after the meeting ends where the tutorial follows the file.

questions.question: Do you want to record this meeting to the computer or to the cloud?
questions.why: The menu offers distinct options to record locally or to the cloud, which determines how and where the final video file is saved.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Letting an agent decide means you lose control over where the recording is stored and the ability to manually pause it during sensitive moments.
questions.check: Which record options does the menu list, and is cloud recording available on this plan?
questions.say_example: Set recording to this computer. Cloud recording isn't on the free plan.

questions.question: Do you want to let this recording extension read and change your data on every website?
questions.why: The browser popup explicitly warns that installing this extension gives it broad access to read and change your data across all websites.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to evaluate the privacy and security risks of giving a third-party extension broad access to your browsing data.
questions.check: What permissions does the extension's install prompt ask for?
questions.say_example: This site has no built-in recording. The <tl;dv> extension would do it, but it asks to read and change your data on every website. Install it, or skip the recording?

questions.question: Do you want to start recording the meeting?
questions.why: The 'More actions' menu displays the 'Start recording' option, allowing you to capture the live meeting for future reference.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide whether the meeting's content is appropriate or necessary to record.
questions.check: Does the page show a recording indicator, and a notice that participants are being told?
questions.say_example: Recording started. Everyone in the call gets a notice that they're being recorded.

questions.question: Do you want to stop recording the meeting?
questions.why: The system displays a confirmation dialog asking if you are sure you want to stop the active recording.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide exactly when the conversation should go off the official record.
questions.check: Does the dialog ask to confirm stopping the recording?
questions.say_example: Stopped the recording. The file is saving.

questions.question: Do you want to pause or stop the active recording?
questions.why: The recording controls display both 'Pause Recording' and 'Stop Recording' buttons, which dictate whether the current capture is temporarily suspended or permanently finalized.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide whether to temporarily halt the recording or finalize the recording file completely.
questions.check: Does the page show 'Pause recording' and 'Stop recording' controls?
questions.say_example: Paused the recording, as you asked.

questions.question: Where do you want to save the converted recording files?
questions.why: The screen showed a 'Save my recordings at:' dialog asking to confirm or change the local destination path.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to choose a specific folder for their recording, potentially making the file hard to find later.
questions.check: What path does the 'Save my recordings at' dialog show?
questions.say_example: Left recordings saving to <Documents/Zoom>.

questions.question: Did the recording link actually appear in the meeting chat as the banner promised?
questions.why: Checking the chat thread confirms that the system fulfilled the banner's promise to deliver the stopped recording.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the immediate reassurance of personally confirming that the meeting recording was successfully generated and saved.
questions.check: After the recording stopped, does the chat show a link to the recording?
questions.say_example: The banner promised the recording link in chat. It hasn't shown up after <two> minutes. Look in <Drive> for it later.

questions.question: Do you want the recording downloaded, or just its link saved?
questions.why: The tl;dv recording page displays the captured video, transcript, and icons to download or copy the link, requiring a choice on how to distribute the file.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the ability to personally decide who receives the recording link or whether the file is downloaded for your own secure records.
questions.check: Does the recording page show download and copy-link options?
questions.say_example: Noted the recording link. It's in the notes for you.

questions.question: Do you want to wait for the recording to finish converting and check the files?
questions.why: The screen shows a conversion progress dialog, which must finish before the final video and audio files are accessible in your local file manager.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to immediately verify the recording files and organize them into your preferred local folder.
questions.check: Does the page show a conversion progress dialog, and has it finished?
questions.say_example: Waited for the recording to convert. Files are in <Documents/Zoom>.

children.label: Leave or end the meeting
children.note: 9.1 on every host that ends on camera - End meeting for all every time in the corpus. 9.2 where the product confirms - Zoom asks and Meet does not. 9.3 on Meet after any leave. 9.4 loops back to 5 - d8L2 from the left-screen and 3Og- and wGXI by starting over.

questions.question: Do you want to leave the meeting now?
questions.why: The meeting control bar features a prominent red 'Leave' button with a phone icon that immediately disconnects you from the live session.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the ability to decide exactly when to conclude your presence and exit the conversation.
questions.check: Does the control bar show a Leave button?
questions.say_example: Left the meeting, as you asked.

questions.question: Should you end the meeting for everyone or just leave?
questions.why: The dialog presents a choice between ending the meeting for all or just leaving, which determines if the session stays open for other participants.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means the agent might abruptly terminate the call for everyone instead of letting the remaining participants continue.
questions.check: Does the dialog offer 'End meeting for all' and 'Leave meeting'?
questions.say_example: You're the host. Leave and let it keep running, or end it for everyone? Say leave or end.

questions.question: Do you want to rate the call quality, or just return to the home screen?
questions.why: The post-meeting screen displays a star rating prompt for audio and video quality alongside the option to return to the home screen.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to provide feedback on their specific call experience to the platform.
questions.check: Does the post-call screen show a rating prompt and a home button?
questions.say_example: Skipped the rating and went back to the home screen.

questions.question: Do you want to rejoin after landing on the 'left the meeting' screen?
questions.why: The screen displays options to rejoin, return to the home screen, or submit feedback, requiring a choice to recover from the interruption.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to decide whether to immediately rejoin the meeting or abandon the attempt after being disconnected.
questions.check: Does the page show 'You left the meeting' or 'You've been disconnected' with a rejoin button?
questions.say_example: The call dropped. Rejoining now.
